newsitem.title: FRANCE: Cerus stock jumps on buyout bid report.
newsitem.headline: Cerus stock jumps on buyout bid report.

text.p: Shares in Cerus, Italian industrialist Carlo De Benedetti's French holding company, shot up on Monday on a report that he was in talks to sell Cerus to the French company CGIP.

Both Cerus and CGIP declined to comment on the report in the French newspaper Les Echos, which said such a deal would solve the longstanding dilemma of how to keep car parts maker Valeo, controlled by Cerus, from falling into foreign hands.
It would also ease some of De Benedetti's woes by providing cash for his debt-laden CIR and Cofide companies. Cofide holds 46 percent of CIR, which in turn holds 49 percent of Cerus.
De Benedetti last week stepped down as chairman of Italy's Olivetti after failing to turn the company around.
He had previously sought to raise cash by seeking a buyer for Cerus's stake in Valeo, a thriving car equipment company seen as the jewel in Cerus's crown.
But French authorities and the two French car companies PSA Peugeot Citroen and Renault expressed alarm at the prospect of Valeo falling under foreign control.
U.S. companies General Motors and TRW Inc were both reported to be keenly interested in Valeo.
Industry Minister Franck Borotra last week said he hoped a "French solution" to the problem of Valeo's ownership would be found this month.
Shares in Cerus were suspended twice in early trading before settling off their peaks at 128.70 francs at midday, up eight percent from their close on Friday.

The newspaper said a price of around 170 francs per share for Cerus might satisfy all parties. At that price, Cerus would be worth 5.8 billion francs, but the price would have to take into account separately Valeo's worth and Cerus's debts.
Shares in CGIP dipped on Monday as did Valeo's stock. La Tribune said Valeo would be priced at around 350 francs per share.
It said the deal would be engineered to avoid a takeover bid for Valeo by transferring Cerus's 28 percent capital stake in Valeo to CGIP but not its 42 percent voting rights.
The report said CGIP may sell one of its industrial stakes -- it has minority holdings in Crown Cork & Seal, Cap Gemini and Wheeklabrato-Allevard -- to finance the deal.
It said CGIP chairman Erneste-Antoine Seilliere was a member of Valeo's board and a longtime associate of De Benedetti, having backed his bid in 1986 to buy into Valeo.
